authored_explainer.title: Cereal Production Rose 1.5x Instead of Running Out
authored_explainer.hook: Food was supposed to run out; cereal production rose 1.5x instead.
says: Progression to secondary school rose from 77.8% in 1985 to 91.3% in 2017 — 1.2 times higher.
Cereal production climbed from 1083.7 million metric tons in 1972 to 1644.1 million in 2024 — 1.5 times higher.
Farmland spans China 5.2, United States 4.2, Australia 3.6, Brazil 2.4, and Russia 2.2 million square kilometers.
authored_explainer.closing: Food output grew while the biggest farmland totals stayed concentrated in five countries.
authored_explainer.question: What changed food production most?

authored_explainer.title: Waste Energy Is 3.0x Higher Than In 1990
authored_explainer.hook: The fastest-growing source here is the stuff we throw away.
says: Combustible renewables and waste rose from 10.2% in 1990 to 30.1% in 2024 — 3.0 times higher.
Electricity access rose from 73.2% in 1998 to 91.9% in 2024 — 1.3 times higher.
Waste methane rose from 903.8 Mt CO2e in 1972 to 1,652 Mt CO2e in 2024 — 1.8 times higher.
authored_explainer.closing: Turning waste into fuel does not erase its growing methane cost.
authored_explainer.question: Should waste energy count as clean?

authored_explainer.title: Population Growth Fell 54% Since 1972
authored_explainer.hook: Population growth was supposed to accelerate; it fell 54% instead.
says: Rural population fell from 63.1% in 1972 to 42.2% in 2025 — down to 67 percent of that.
Largest-city population shifted from 18.2% in 1972 to 16.2% in 2025 — it barely moved.
Population growth fell from 2% in 1972 to 0.91% in 2025 — down to 46 percent of that.
authored_explainer.closing: Slower growth still adds people, but it changes what cities must prepare for.
authored_explainer.question: How should cities plan now?
